task: Phase C: engine-vs-engine cross-check of the simulation lane -- NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 (sim-capacity) vs hftbacktest 2.4.4 (sim-crosscheck-hftbacktest), replaying one shared deterministic order stream over one bounded, already-retained Alpaca SIP sample.

repair_round.reason: An independent adversarial review of the first attempt (commit d5cc0c58) refuted its conclusion outright. This receipt is the corrected replacement, produced from a fixed driver and re-verified independently (not merely re-typed from the review). The first attempt's exact content, hashes and root cause are preserved at receipts/20260925-crosscheck-superseded.json -- kept on record, not deleted -- and summarized in superseded_first_attempt below.

claim_boundary: This is an engine-execution-semantics comparison only, on a fixture-scoped, non-reactive order stream -- it is infrastructure/methodology evidence, never strategy evidence and never a broker-throughput claim (docs/harness-rules-convergence-20260922.md NS-06; sim-capacity/README.md's claim_boundary). No order here reacts to price direction, volatility or any signal.

superseded_first_attempt.verdict: WRONG. Refuted by an independent adversarial review; the refutation was independently reproduced by this repair round, not merely trusted.
superseded_first_attempt.root_cause: Use-after-free in the original run_hftbacktest.py (lines 126-128 at commit d5cc0c58): a single loop-local `data` variable was reassigned once per symbol inside the per-symbol BacktestAsset-build loop. `BacktestAsset.add_data(data)` does not take ownership of the numpy array or increment its refcount -- it stores a raw pointer into the array's own buffer (py-hftbacktest/hftbacktest/__init__.py:119-120 passes the buffer address; lib.rs:206-210 wraps it with DataPtr::from_ptr; backtest/data/mod.rs's own comment on that pointer type says it is "not owned ... must remain valid"). As soon as the SECOND symbol's array was built, the FIRST symbol's (NVDA, built first since sorted alphabetically before SPY) only Python reference was gone, and CPython was free to reclaim that memory while hftbacktest's Rust side kept reading through the now-dangling pointer for the rest of the run.
superseded_first_attempt.reviewer_reported_evidence: 72,134 of 74,835 NVDA (asset 0) event bytes differed in memory after a short elapse; 0 of SPY's (asset 1, built last, so never reassigned-away) bytes changed. Reruns on identical input gave 385, 380 and 385 fills. One run hung for more than 16 minutes; a two-symbol synthetic run segfaulted. With the arrays kept alive: NVDA fills 699/720 at 70ms and 674/720 at 250ms, touch share 100%, partial_fill and no_partial_fill agree on 1439/1439 orders. Against Nautilus: -0.21% at 70ms and 0.00% at 250ms. A last-NBBO-crossing oracle predicts NVDA 701/720 at 70ms; Nautilus agrees with it on 99.58% of orders.

determinism_check_against_the_unmodified.method: git show d5cc0c58:blueprints/us-equities/sim-engine-crosscheck/run_hftbacktest.py, run run_stream(quotes, stream, latency_ms=70, exchange='partial_fill') twice with no code changes
determinism_check_against_the_unmodified.conclusion: Confirms non-determinism directly: identical input, identical unmodified code, two different outcome sets.

isolation_check_against_the_unmodified_o.method: same old driver: NVDA run alone vs NVDA's own outcomes extracted from a two-symbol (NVDA+SPY) run
isolation_check_against_the_unmodified_o.conclusion: Confirms cross-symbol contamination: the SAME symbol's outcomes differ depending on whether another symbol's array was built afterward in the same call, which should be impossible for correctly isolated per-asset data.

withdrawn_findings: F1 ("NVDA fill-rate gap driven by Nautilus's latency-release-on-next-quote-or-timer semantics interacting with NVDA's sparser quotes") -- WITHDRAWN. The ~82% NVDA relative divergence F1 tried to explain never existed as a real engine difference; it was corrupted-memory output on the hftbacktest side. With the fix, NVDA fill rate agrees within 0.43% (70ms) between the two engines (see metrics_table below).

F2 ("hftbacktest's own PartialFillExchange vs NoPartialFillExchange disagree on NVDA at 70ms, a suspected hftbacktest-internal inconsistency") -- WITHDRAWN. This was the identical use-after-free, not a real hftbacktest behavior: with the fix, the two exchange models agree on 1439/1439 orders (byte-identical outcomes) at both latencies (see with_the_fix_applied_same_two_checks and metrics_table).

fix.use_after_free: Every per-symbol event array is now appended to a `_data_arrays` list held alive for the whole `run_stream` call (through `hbt.close()`), so no array's Python reference count can reach zero while hftbacktest still holds a raw pointer into it. See run_hftbacktest.py's module docstring for the full citation trail.
fix.exact_submit_times: Orders are now submitted at their exact scheduled `ts_ns` (the engine's clock is `elapse()`d directly to each order's own time, computed as a delta from `hbt.current_timestamp`) instead of the original 10ms polling grid.
fix.exec_qty_source: Filled quantity is now read as `qty - leaves_qty` (the order's own before/after bookkeeping), not `exec_qty`, which upstream holds only the LAST individual fill call's quantity -- irrelevant for the single-tick-fill case this dataset exercises once the corruption is fixed, but was masking the corruption's true footprint in the original run.
verified_by: two-symbol vs single-symbol isolation: hash-identical (see independently_reproduced_this_round)
oracle agreement >=99% for every engine and every symbol (see oracle_agreement)
zero better-than-touch violations across all 8 runs (see better_than_touch_violations)

locked_quote_rows_measured_this_round.note: Locked quotes (bid == ask): HashMapMarketDepth::update_bid_depth/update_ask_depth each independently enforce best_bid < best_ask (hashmapmarketdepth.rs ~177-182); whichever side's DEPTH_EVENT is applied second at a locked price wins, evicting the other side's touch from the book until the next event restores it. Measured (independently recounted this round, matching the review exactly) to affect one order's outcome across the whole 8-run configuration matrix. This is real, disclosed upstream depth-model behavior on a locked L1 book, not a bug, and unrelated to the use-after-free.

hftbacktest_exchange_model_agreement.conclusion: partial_fill_exchange and no_partial_fill_exchange produce byte-identical outcomes on every order at both latencies, once the use-after-free is fixed.

oracle_agreement.method: oracle.py: last NBBO at or before submit_ts + latency, limit crosses, top-of-book size >= qty -- independent of both engines, computed from the retained quotes alone.
oracle_agreement.interpretation: hftbacktest's constant-latency, last-NBBO-crossing model matches the oracle's own definition almost by construction (100% in every configuration -- a strong sanity check the fix is correct, not merely a coincidence). NautilusTrader's default (non-exact) configuration is 99.65-99.72%; its exact_latency variant is closer still (99.72-99.93%) -- the residual gap from 100% is the release-timing finding below, not a matching bug.

better_than_touch_violations.note: metrics.better_than_touch_violations, run as a hard check inside crosscheck.py report -- report generation itself raises and aborts on any violation, for either engine. The first attempt never ran this check against hftbacktest's own output; it would have caught the use-after-free directly (354 of 384 NVDA fills in that broken run were better than any displayed quote, by up to 87 cents; buys 53/360, sells 331/360).

release_timing_finding.summary: A real, minor, disclosed NautilusTrader property, distinct from the withdrawn F1/F2 and from the hftbacktest fix: a deferred order is released only when some event (its own instrument's next quote, or any due clock timer) is next processed at or after submit + latency, not exactly at that instant. With this cross-check's own single, shared 3/sec submit-schedule timer as the only per-order timer, an order can sit past its configured latency until the next actual trigger -- adding extra, instrument-dependent delay.
release_timing_finding.reviewer_reported_for_comparison: median 28.0ms (SPY) / 53.4ms (NVDA), p90 135ms/263ms -- this task's own independent recomputation is close (small differences consistent with percentile-interpolation method), not identical, and corroborates the same magnitude and NVDA > SPY pattern.
release_timing_finding.tested_fix: exact_latency=True (one no-op time alert per order at submit + latency, run_nautilus.py) makes every filled order resolve at EXACTLY submit + latency (verified directly: min/max extra delay both exactly 0.0ms in every exact_latency run) and brings NVDA fill rate to 699/720 (97.08%) at 70ms, versus hftbacktest's 701/720 (97.36%) -- a 0.29% relative difference, versus the primary (non-exact) comparison's already-small 0.43%.
release_timing_finding.classification: A real, minor NautilusTrader timing-realism property (not optimism -- see prices_near_touch below), independent of and much smaller than either withdrawn finding. Not attributed to sim-capacity's own exerciser as a defect within THIS task's scope.
release_timing_finding.prices_near_touch: Nautilus's actual fill prices, even when resolved later than submit + latency, stay within the touch_share_pct=100.0 guarantee (see metrics_table) -- the extra delay affects WHEN an order resolves, not that it fills through a stale or better-than-touch price.
release_timing_finding.recommendation: Fix sim-capacity's own CapacityExerciser/runner timing (e.g. an equivalent per-order release alert, or documenting the release-timing behavior explicitly) in a SEPARATE follow-up PR. Not done in this task, which does not change sim-capacity code.

overturn_evaluation.condition_verbatim_from_sim_capacity_exp: Cross-check the same fetched data through hftbacktest 2.4.4/rust 0.9.4 (MIT, catalogued at 5f3ec40b2afb764e0fea112f941ed85523ef4e88) and compare fill rate / median time-to-fill; overturn if it diverges from this record's NautilusTrader results by more than 20% or 2x with no attributable Nautilus matching bug.
overturn_evaluation.conclusion: AGREES WITHIN TOLERANCE. Neither threshold in the overturn condition is met (0.30-0.36% fill-rate divergence, far under 20%; 1.16-1.59x median time-to-fill, under 2x), so the "no attributable Nautilus matching bug" clause is moot -- the condition simply does not trigger. The sim-capacity NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 destination is NOT overturned by this cross-check. This corrects the first attempt's (withdrawn) conclusion, which reported a 27-29% fill-rate divergence caused entirely by the hftbacktest driver's own use-after-free, not by either engine's real behavior.
